description: The team of gecw who are passionate about technology
summary: Team GECW built an interactive website that helps choose Earth test sites for Mars and Moon rovers. It covers 16 sites (8 for each world) on a satellite map. Each site has an estimated match score, numbered test zones, a simulated rover drive, comparisons with known test sites and real places on Mars and the Moon, and photos. A ranking of the team’s best picks puts Qaidam Basin first for Mars and Lonar Crater first for the Moon, and visitors can add any place to compare it with the rest. All scores are estimates, to be confirmed with elevation and satellite data, and the next step is adding real slope data from our Python program.
details: Our project tackles a basic problem in space robotics: rovers can’t be tested on Mars or the Moon before launch, so engineers test them on Earth at “analog” sites whose ground resembles those worlds, and picking the right site is hard because each test, such as long-range driving, soft sand, steep slopes, crater descents or fine dust, needs different terrain. To help, our team built an interactive website that lets anyone explore and compare 16 candidate sites, 8 for Mars and 8 for the Moon, on a satellite map. For each site it shows an estimated match score, the reasons the place resembles Mars or the Moon, and numbered test zones that each show what a rover could prove there. A visitor can send a simulated rover along a planned route that stops at each zone and logs what it tests. The site also compares each place with well-known test sites such as Atacama, Mauna Kea and Iceland, and with real locations like Jezero Crater and Shackleton crater. It shows satellite views and photos, and it ranks the team’s best picks using a score of 70% match, 15% easy access and 15% track record. A visitor can also type in any place name to have the site look up its elevation, climate and description online and compare it with every site. The result is a single web page that turns a complicated site-selection question into something a beginner can explore, with ratings that are clearly marked as estimates to be confirmed with satellite elevation data.
